title: 2 Iris paths mis-owned; no proposal kind exists to fix them
body:
Ran lint() + resolve() against the live map (~/iris-workplace/map.yaml + org.yaml) for the 9 paths flagged by ft_mummakwyuew19.

Findings:
- 7/9 already resolve correctly, matching the suggested scheme: media.py, experts/media.py, experts/device.py → experts; stt_stream.py, speaker.py → conversation; desktop/character/driver.js, conversation.js → character. No change needed.
- 2 are genuinely mis-owned: services/agent-svc/voice_native.py and wake_listen.py fall back to "experts" (the agent-svc directory default) instead of "conversation" (where stt/voice/wake/speaker belongs).
- Full lint found nothing else unowned — only one unrelated warning (mobile-android has no holder).

Blocker: propose_org_change's six kinds (hire/retire/split/merge/reassign/restructure) have no way to add or move a single path entry between two existing charters. "reassign" only moves which employee holds a charter; split/merge only operate on whole charters and split can't target an already-existing charter (throws "already exists"). I checked proposals.ts directly — this isn't a usage error, the capability isn't there. I also have no write path to map.yaml myself (it's outside my worktree's allowed paths), so I can't fix it by hand either.

Recommendation: approve a one-off direct edit adding exactly 2 entries (voice_native.py, wake_listen.py → primary: conversation) — smallest possible fix, no new charter. Longer-term, proposals.ts could get a small "remap-paths" kind for cases like this, but that's jkj server code change, separate decision.

newCharter.mission: Detect and expose facts about the user's environment and device state — screen/share content, meeting or call presence, weather, and future sources like calendar or location — through the existing context query interface, so any charter can read a fact without building its own sensor.
explicitlyNotOwned: how a fact is used once read (the Speaker/delivery gate, character voice, proactive triggers) — stays with conversation/character
raw OS-level controls like mic mute UI or desktop permissions — stays with desktop-mac/mobile; context-provider owns exposing the resulting state as a context fact, not the control surface itself
